professional: a quantitative methodologist in computational social science / a statistician who works on selective inference and text-as-data. They would check first that the label and corpus are built as stated, that the held-out z tests and BH step are the textbook ones, that the 'overstatement' ratio measures what it says (selection bias, not noise), that the shuffled-label control is calibrated, that the tokens being tested are real words, and what the nearest prior work (Ludwig and Mullainathan 2024; Fightin' Words; winner's-curse literature; LLM distribution-difference describers) already shows

evidence.correctness: Reran experiments/run.py in a scratch copy (it writes results.txt, so not in the tree; needs qual-real and qual-correction on the path): 43.6 s, results.txt byte-identical to the committed one, figure.py regenerates replication.svg byte-identical. Independent recomputation (scratchpad qual/indep.py, imports nothing from the subject): pandas load of goemotions_1.csv, own rater collapse with the GoEmotions paper's 11 negative emotions -> 5,313 examples, share 0.2469 (README 5,313 / 0.247); the E3 split rebuilt from the same seeded permutation, counted with own code, tested with statsmodels proportions_ztest (pooled) and multipletests fdr_bh: all 20 words, discovery effects, held-out effects, p values and replicated flags equal results.txt E3 to the printed precision. Author's BH vs statsmodels fdr_bh on 20,000 random 20-p families: 0 disagreements. Shuffled-label control: 11/200 at n=2000 has Wilson 95% 3.1-9.6%, pooled 27/800 = 3.4% (2.3-4.9%), so 'consistent with 5%' holds. Ratios 0.0948/0.0125 = 7.58 and 0.0211/0.0141 = 1.50 as printed. What keeps it from 4: the computations are right but the headline quantity is not the one it is named for (claims/domain): the mean ABSOLUTE held-out effect includes the noise floor (0.0089 with shuffled labels at n=100); the in-direction (signed) held-out effect at n=100 is 0.0023 (probe, 100 splits), so discovery effects are about 40x too large there, not 7.6x; at n=2000 signed 0.0139 vs abs 0.0143, so the 1.5x stands. 3.

evidence.verification: `cd research/qual-hypothesis && python3 -m unittest test_qualhyp`: 7 tests OK in 0.003 s. Seven mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: caught 3 (restates_label without emotion names; pooled p -> a/n1; BH cut off-by-one). Survived 4: BH replaced by Bonferroni (alpha*rank/m -> alpha/m) survives because test_bh's family [0.001, 0.2, 0.9, 0.012] gives the same answer under both (0.012 <= 0.0125); dropping the same-sign requirement for replication; min_count >= -> >; ranking by |d| instead of |z|. No test pins any experiment number (results.txt) or the shuffled-label calibration. 2.
evidence.craft: Read qualhyp.py (91 lines), test_qualhyp.py, experiments/run.py, figure.py, and the imported qual-real/qualreal.py loader and tokenizer. Small, readable, stdlib, seeded, pure functions. Defects: the tokenizer `[a-z']+` (qual-real/qualreal.py:22) does not normalise U+2019, so 'I’m', 'don’t' split into 'm', 't', 'don' (673 of 5,313 comments contain U+2019); three of E3's 20 hypotheses are such fragments and 'm' is reported as a confirmed hypothesis. Cross-project sys.path imports (qualhyp.py:13, run.py:13-14) into qual-real and transitively qual-correction; `import random` unused in qualhyp.py:9; restates_label rebuilds set(r.NEGATIVE) per call. 3.
evidence.claims: Backed: 5,313 comments and 24.7% (recomputed), 0.8 -> 14.7 replicating, shuffled 0.03-0.07 and at most 5.5% of splits (results.txt, rerun), 36-59% label vocabulary at 300-2,000 (results.txt), E3 word list (recomputed), 'not an LLM' disclosed prominently, references flagged as from memory, no comment text committed (checked: no CSV in the tree). Not backed as worded: the headline 'overstates every effect ... 7.6 times too large' (README:3, project.json summary, live page) uses mean |held-out effect| as the truth; that is inflated by noise, and the signed held-out effect gives ~40x at 100 comments; README:62 'mean held-out difference about 1 point' is the same absolute measure (the signed one at n=100 is 0.2 points). 'overstates every effect' is a statement about a mean, not each of the 20. 'm' and 'lol' are discussed as hypotheses without saying 'm' is a tokenizer fragment of I’m. 2.
evidence.fitness: A researcher wanting to test LLM-proposed hypotheses could reuse test_hypotheses/benjamini_hochberg and the split harness (small and correct), but the thing the project is about, an LLM proposer, is absent, the hypotheses are single tokens, and the restatement measure is a hand list. Nearest prior work: Ludwig and Mullainathan (QJE 2024), cited, already does generate-then-validate on held-out data with a far richer proposer; word-level discriminative lexicons with held-out checks are Monroe, Colaresi and Quinn's 'Fightin' Words' (Political Analysis 2008), not cited; the winner's curse after selection is standard (Zhong and Prentice 2008; Ioannidis 2008), cited only via an internal project; LLM describers of distribution differences with held-out validation (Zhong et al. 2022 D5, ICML; Zhou et al. 2024 HypoGeniC) not cited. Result: sound in direction, not new, below a publishable contribution. 2.
evidence.domain: Against selective-inference practice: sample splitting plus BH on the selected family is the textbook remedy and is implemented correctly; the shuffled-label control checks only the complete null (FWER), not FDR under a mixture of true and null hypotheses, which needs planted effects. The inflation measure departs from practice (compare in-direction held-out estimates, or the conditional/bias-corrected estimator, not absolute values). 'Restates the label' should be a conditional test (README's own next step) rather than a list. Tokens should be normalised before treating them as hypotheses. 2.

verdict: A small, honest, correctly computed milestone. Everything it prints reproduces bit for bit (results.txt and the SVG), and an independent pandas/statsmodels pipeline that imports none of its code rebuilds the 5,313-comment corpus, the 24.7% label and all 20 rows of the E3 split exactly; its BH equals statsmodels on 20,000 families and the shuffled-label control is calibrated (27/800, Wilson 2.3-4.9%). It does not meet the bar: the headline '7.6 times too large' divides by the mean absolute held-out effect, which at 100 discovery comments is mostly noise (signed held-out effect 0.0023, so the inflation is ~40x); 4 of 7 seeded bugs survive, including BH replaced by Bonferroni, because the one BH test case cannot tell them apart; three of the E3 hypotheses are curly-apostrophe fragments ('m', 't', 'don'); and the result (winner's curse plus a held-out BH check, with a word-count proposer instead of an LLM) is a known one, short of the nearest prior work (Ludwig and Mullainathan 2024, Fightin' Words) and of a PhD-level contribution. Finished for what it claims (completeness 3), below the bar on claims, verification, fitness and domain.
